title: Blender 5.3 released with Gaussian Splat support
why_read: A concrete, useful feature release for a major open-source 3D tool, relevant to graphics and VFX practitioners.
analysis: Blender 5.3 adding native Gaussian Splat support means the open-source 3D suite can now import, render, and likely edit these increasingly popular radiance-field-based 3D scene representations. Gaussian splatting is a newer technique for photorealistic scene reconstruction from photos or video, competing with NeRFs but much faster to render. Having this in a mainstream tool like Blender lowers the barrier for artists and researchers to incorporate captured real-world scenes into traditional 3D pipelines. Relevant to graphics engineers and anyone tracking the maturation of this rendering technique.
